newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar drifts rangebound before expiry.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar drifts rangebound before expiry.

text.p: Activity on London's white sugar market reflected the dull performance seen earlier in Thursday's session as the December/March spread dominated interest and traders rolled spot positions forward before expiry.
Mixed buying in the second-month March kept values supported but activity was subdued, traders said.

"There's good support in the March and that's about it," said one. Volume was on the light side at 1706 GMT and amounted to 1,332 lots. December was just 20 cents lower at $303.50, just above the intraday low. March was 70 cents higher at $304.00.

Fresh physical news was thin on the ground, despite market expectations that the lower futures prices would lure buyers. Poland is likely to be an origin for deliveries against the December expiry, traders said.
Technically, March is remaining within a major downtrend channel dating from mid-September with initial resistance pegged at $304 followed by $306 from the trendline.
Analysts said the March contract -- where open interest is now concentrated -- would probably attempt to consolidate after its recent weakness as values were quite heavily oversold.
Paris positions were slightly firmer in a scant overall volume of 310 lots. December was untraded and March up 50 cents at $304.00.
